title: The Enactive Approach to Architectural Experience: A Neurophysiological Perspective on Embodiment, Motivation, and Affordances
central_proposition: The enactive approach provides a systematic neuroscientific and phenomenological framework for understanding architectural experience as an embodied, motivated, and affordance-driven interaction between human beings and the built environment, thereby informing user-centered design.

concept_definitions.name: Enaction
concept_definitions.definition: A living being is an autonomous agent that actively generates and maintains its own cognitive domain through continuous reciprocal interactions of the brain, body, and the world.

concept_definitions.name: Sense-making
concept_definitions.definition: The process by which living organisms, as self-individuating and sense-producing systems, engage with the world, transforming it into a place of salience, meaning, and value, understood as a bodily cognitive-emotional form of understanding.

concept_definitions.name: Constitutive Relatedness
concept_definitions.definition: The intrinsic coupling between cognition, body, and the world, where a cognitive being's experiential world is a relational domain enacted by its autonomous agency and mode of coupling with the environment.

concept_definitions.name: Embodied Action
concept_definitions.definition: Cognition defined as an exercise of skillful know-how by an embodied and situationally embedded agent, modulated by sensorimotor patterns through bodily interactions with the environment.

concept_definitions.name: Sensorimotor Contingencies
concept_definitions.definition: The regularities in which sensory stimulation changes with movement, forming the basis of implicit know-how in perception.

concept_definitions.name: Body Schema
concept_definitions.definition: A continuously updating neural representation of the body's configuration, posture, and movement, functioning as a set of dynamic sensorimotor principles that organize perception and action, including interoceptive emotional inputs. It provides a pre-reflective consciousness of oneself as an experiencing, lived body and acts as a 'power for action'.

concept_definitions.name: Affordances
concept_definitions.definition: Possibilities for action provided by an environment to an animal, conceived as relations between the abilities of animals and features of the environment, and understood as value-rich potentialities of interaction emerging in an agent's perception.

concept_definitions.name: Immersion (in VR)
concept_definitions.definition: The device's ability to induce a high degree of 'immersion' within the virtual world, based on the number and range of user's sensory and motor channels connected to the system.

concept_definitions.name: Presence (in VR)
concept_definitions.definition: The strong feeling of 'being physically present' in the perceived virtual environment, reflected in modulation of psychophysiological and neurophysiological responses.

argument_structure: The paper first establishes the historical context of architecture's concern for human well-being and the recent emergence of neuroscience for architecture. It then introduces the enactive approach as a solution to the 'disembodied observer' problem, detailing its core tenets: sense-making, constitutive relatedness, and embodied action. It elaborates on the sensorimotor theory of perception and the crucial role of body schema, linking these to phenomenological concepts. Next, it integrates the concept of affordances, arguing that architecture designs these possibilities for action, which are enacted through body schema. Finally, it proposes Immersive Virtual Reality (IVR) as a valuable tool for empirically investigating these enactive principles in architectural experience, citing existing VR research on presence, emotion, and embodiment.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: Architectural experience is an active, dynamic interaction shaped by the organism's embodied nature. The specific features of the human body (sensorimotor capacities, posture, internal states) determine perception and interaction. Perception is action-oriented, with the brain predicting sensory consequences of motor actions and updating body schema. Architectural elements trigger implicit sensorimotor knowledge, guiding movement and shaping spatial understanding. Interoceptive emotional inputs and motivational states influence perceptual attunement and direct actions, contributing to sense-making and valuation. Architectural design creates 'affordances' (possibilities for action) that are perceived and 'enacted' through the body schema, meaning the environment invites and organizes behavior based on bodily capabilities and motivations. This establishes a two-way dependence: architecture expresses human embodiment and influences human experience. In immersive VR, natural sensory-motor interaction leads to 'presence,' eliciting realistic physiological and emotional responses, allowing empirical investigation of these mechanisms.

findings.mechanism: Living beings are autonomous agents that actively generate and maintain their own cognitive domain through continuous reciprocal interactions with the environment.
findings.source: The Enactive Approach to Cognition and Experience: General Framework
findings.quote: a living being is an autonomous agent that actively generates and maintains its own cognitive domain through continuous reciprocal interactions

findings.mechanism: Living systems engage with the world in a manner that transforms it into a place of salience, meaning, and value, due to a fundamental 'lack of indifference' (primordial affectivity).
findings.source: The Enactive Approach to Cognition and Experience: General Framework
findings.quote: they engage with the world in such manner that these interactions transform the world into a place of salience, meaning, and value

findings.mechanism: Sense-making is a bodily cognitive-emotional form of understanding, where the organism as a whole is a vehicle of meaning.
findings.source: The Enactive Approach to Cognition and Experience: General Framework
findings.quote: sense-making can be more accurately described as a bodily cognitive-emotional form of understanding

findings.mechanism: Whatever a being is able to experience, know, and practically handle is determined and shaped by the particular features of that being's body.
findings.source: The Enactive Approach to Cognition and Experience: General Framework
findings.quote: whatever a being is able to experience, know, and practically handle is determined and shaped by the particular features of that being's body

findings.mechanism: The co-constitution of the perceiving agent and the world (architecture) is made apparent by understanding the modes of human embodiment as a living-lived body.
findings.source: The Enactive Approach to Cognition and Experience: General Framework
findings.quote: this co-constitution of the perceiving agent and the world (or more specifically, architecture) can be made apparent by understanding the modes of embodiment

findings.mechanism: Visual experience is the activity of exploring the world mediated by the knowledge of sensorimotor contingencies, i.e., understanding implicitly the regularities in which sensory stimulation changes with movement.
findings.source: Sensorimotor Theory of Perception and Experience of Architecture
findings.quote: visual experience is the activity of exploring the world which is mediated by the knowledge of sensorimotor contingencies

findings.mechanism: Perceptual openness depends not only on the mastery of sensorimotor contingencies but also on preconscious affective and motivational states, which are intrinsic components of action-perception cycles.
findings.source: Sensorimotor Theory of Perception and Experience of Architecture
findings.quote: our perceptual openness to the world (i.e., what we can perceive at any instance in time) depends not only on the mastery of sensorimotor contingencies, but also on our preconscious affective, motivational states

findings.mechanism: Basic architectural experiences have a 'verb form' because architecture initiates, directs, and organizes behavior and movement, reflecting an embodied nature and perceptual attunement.
findings.source: Sensorimotor Theory of Perception and Experience of Architecture
findings.quote: basic architectural experiences have a verb form because architecture initiates, directs, and organizes behavior and movement

findings.mechanism: Body schema is a functional mechanism that organizes the intrinsic constitutive coupling between perception, action, and emotion, enabling one's capacity to act coherently and be aware of one's own body.
findings.source: The Role of Body Schema in Architectural Experience
findings.quote: the body schema is a concept extensively used in a variety of disciplines, including neuroscience and psychology, to describe one's capacity to act coherently in the world

findings.mechanism: Body schema plays a fundamental role in providing a minimal sense of self, a pre-reflective consciousness of ourselves as experiencing, lived bodies.
findings.source: The Role of Body Schema in Architectural Experience
findings.quote: body schema plays a fundamental role in providing us with a minimal sense of self—that is, with a pre-reflective consciousness of ourselves as experiencing, lived bodies

findings.mechanism: Body schema includes interoceptive emotional inputs, which serve as motivational propensity for action, influencing the 'why' of perception.
findings.source: The Role of Body Schema in Architectural Experience
findings.quote: body schema includes not only the processes underlying motor activity and the regulation of postural and kinesthetic information, but also the interoceptive emotional inputs as motivational propensity for action
findings.empirical_support_cited: Berlucchi and Aglioti, 2010; Bower and Gallagher, 2013

findings.consequent: Conscious experience of architectural setting and self
findings.mechanism: Architectural spaces can disrupt the habitual, pre-reflective use of space by acting directly on body schema, activating an attentional switch and allowing conscious experience of both the architectural setting and oneself as an experiencing subject.
findings.source: The Role of Body Schema in Architectural Experience
findings.quote: the moment needed to recalculate the body's position and appropriate action is just enough to activate the attentional switch and to allow the visitor to consciously experience both the architectural setting and oneself as an experiencing and bodily subject

findings.mechanism: Aesthetic experience involves the motor system and related embodied mechanisms, leading to activation of motor circuits during the perception of artworks.
findings.source: Neuroscientific Evidence of Action-Perception and Empathy in Aesthetic Experience
findings.quote: several studies demonstrated the activation of motor circuits during the perception of artworks
findings.empirical_support_cited: Freedberg and Gallese, 2007; Di Dio et al., 2007; Umiltà et al., 2012; Sbriscia-Fioretti et al., 2013

findings.mechanism: Aesthetic experience is an embodied phenomenon directly linked to adaptivity, functioning in the service of better coping with the environment.
findings.source: Neuroscientific Evidence of Action-Perception and Empathy in Aesthetic Experience
findings.quote: aesthetic experience is an embodied phenomenon directly linked to adaptivity (...) and that aesthetic perception functions in the service of a better coping with the environment

findings.mechanism: Judging curvilinear spaces as beautiful and pleasant is associated with increased activity of the anterior cingulate cortex, part of the reward circuitry involved in aesthetic processing.
findings.source: Neuroscientific Evidence of Action-Perception and Empathy in Aesthetic Experience
findings.quote: judging the curvilinear spaces as beautiful and pleasant was associated exclusively with increased activity of the ACC

findings.mechanism: Enclosed spaces elicit more avoidance judgments, associated with greater activity in the anterior midcingulate cortex, part of the reward circuitry involved in aesthetic processing.
findings.source: Neuroscientific Evidence of Action-Perception and Empathy in Aesthetic Experience
findings.quote: the second study showed greater activity in the anterior midcingulate cortex in the case of enclosed spaces, which elicited more avoidance judgments overall in comparison to open spaces

findings.consequent: Emotional experiences and conscious awareness of environment and self
findings.mechanism: Interoceptive signals, along with proprioceptive and exteroceptive information, are crucial for complete 'tracing' of one's own bodily states and body's position in space, represented in the insular cortex.
findings.source: Affective Components of Perception
findings.quote: Recent evidence indicated that interoceptive information about bodily states—both bodily and emotional feelings—is represented in the insular cortex, which is thought to be crucial for emotional experiences and conscious awareness of the environment and the self

findings.mechanism: The orbitofrontal cortex signals the actual value of a given stimulus, which varies according to internal preferences and judgments, independently of sensory modality, and is crucial for instantiating behavior and learning.
findings.source: Affective Components of Perception
findings.quote: the orbitofrontal cortex plays the role of signaling the actual value of a given stimulus, which varies according to internal preferences and judgments, independently of sensory modality

findings.mechanism: The left prefrontal cortex plays a role in moderating patterns of activity related to approaching stimuli, reflecting functional frontal asymmetries.
findings.source: Affective Components of Perception
findings.quote: the left prefrontal cortex plays a role in moderating patterns of activity related to approaching stimuli

findings.mechanism: The right hemisphere of the frontal lobe is asymmetrically activated by avoiding stimuli, reflecting functional frontal asymmetries.
findings.source: Affective Components of Perception
findings.quote: the right hemisphere of the frontal lobe is asymmetrically activated by avoiding stimuli

findings.consequent: Object perception and identification of actions
findings.mechanism: Object perception depends on previously encountered multisensory patterns and affective representations, where bodily sensations provide a 'dimension of knowledge' to identify objects and actions according to past bodily reactions.
findings.source: Affective Components of Perception
findings.quote: object perception does not only depend on previously encountered multisensory patterns but also on affective representations, i.e., prior bodily experiences that influenced the internal sensations

findings.mechanism: People's experience of architectural environments is intrinsically structured by the possibilities for action (affordances), which are informed by sensorimotor knowledge and motivational factors.
findings.source: Affordances in Architectural Terms
findings.quote: people's experience of architectural environments is intrinsically structured by the possibilities for action, which is informed from both sensorimotor knowledge and motivational factors

findings.mechanism: The communicative space of architecture-body is described as the conceptual coupling of body schema and affordances as 'enacted' by architectural environments.
findings.source: Affordances in Architectural Terms
findings.quote: the communicative space of architecture-body might be described as the conceptual coupling of body schema and affordances as 'enacted' by architectural environments

findings.mechanism: Body schema provides embodied capabilities for action that correlate with the affordances of the world, establishing a 'practical attunement' with the surrounding environment.
findings.source: Object Perception and Affordances
findings.quote: body schema provides embodied capabilities for action that correlate with the affordances of the world
findings.empirical_support_cited: Gallagher and Zahavi, 2008; Gallese and Sinigaglia, 2010

findings.mechanism: Seeing a manipulable object selectively recruits the same motor resources typically employed during the planning and execution of actions targeting the same objects, mediated by mirror neurons.
findings.source: Object Perception and Affordances
findings.quote: Seeing a manipulable object (e.g., a tool) selectively recruits the same motor resources typically employed during the planning and execution of actions targeting the same objects
findings.empirical_support_cited: Rizzolatti et al., 1997; Gallese and Sinigaglia, 2013

findings.mechanism: The recruitment of grasping motor representations during object perception can be affected by the same spatial constraints that govern the execution of grasping actions.
findings.source: Object Perception and Affordances
findings.quote: spatial constraints affect one's reuse of his/her own action representations

findings.mechanism: The observation of tools, as well as goal and non-goal directed motor action, leads to an extraction of information about potential affordances, which lies in the neuronal population of motor areas.
findings.source: Object Perception and Affordances
findings.quote: the observation of tools, as well as goal and non-goal directed motor action, leads to an extraction of information about potential affordances and this information lies in the neuronal population of motor areas
findings.empirical_support_cited: EEG studies (Creem-Regehr and Lee, 2005; Proverbio, 2012; Rüther et al., 2014)

findings.mechanism: High levels of presence in virtual environments correspond to higher physiological activities, indicating a more realistic and engaging experience.
findings.source: The Sense of Presence Modulates Emotional Response and Interoceptive Activity
findings.quote: high level of presence corresponds to higher physiological activities (HR and SC)
findings.empirical_support_cited: Meehan et al., 2002, 2005; Vecchiato et al., 2015b

findings.mechanism: Presence is a necessary mediator that allows real emotions to be activated by a virtual environment.
findings.source: The Sense of Presence Modulates Emotional Response and Interoceptive Activity
findings.quote: presence is a necessary mediator that allows real emotions to be activated by a virtual environment

findings.mechanism: The emotional valence of the virtual environment affects the emotional state of the user, with interaction in specific environments producing corresponding feelings.
findings.source: The Sense of Presence Modulates Emotional Response and Interoceptive Activity
findings.quote: the interaction with 'anxious' and 'relaxing' virtual environments produced feelings of anxiety and relaxation respectively, and that the emotional states were influenced by the level of presence
findings.empirical_support_cited: Riva et al., 2007; Baños et al., 2004

findings.mechanism: Participants exhibit greater reactivity to stress when performing tasks in an enclosed virtual room, potentially related to limited possibilities for movement and escape.
findings.source: The Sense of Presence Modulates Emotional Response and Interoceptive Activity
findings.quote: participants exhibited greater reactivity to stress when doing the tasks in the enclosed room, which was especially manifested in the cortisol reactivity

findings.mechanism: The subjective feeling of presence in immersive 3D scenarios is reflected in enhanced frontal-midline theta activity, correlated with spatial navigation success and focused attention.
findings.source: Neuroelectrical Correlates of Sensorimotor Activity and Embodiment
findings.quote: the sense of presence (measured by questionnaire) was reflected in the activation of the frontal-midline theta over a brain network
findings.empirical_support_cited: Vecchiato et al., 2015b; Slobounov et al., 2015

findings.antecedent: Familiar, comfortable, and pleasant virtual environments
findings.mechanism: The recognition of familiar features and perception of comfort/pleasantness in the environment activate cerebral circuits involved in internalized attention, relaxation, and sensorimotor integration.
findings.source: Neuroelectrical Correlates of Sensorimotor Activity and Embodiment
findings.quote: FM-theta was elicited during the visuospatial exploration of environments judged as more familiar, comfortable, and pleasant

findings.mechanism: Architectural interiors modulate bodily self-consciousness through visuo-tactile mechanisms, where the experience of architecture relates to induced changes of bodily self-awareness and identification with the spatial void.
findings.source: Neuroelectrical Correlates of Sensorimotor Activity and Embodiment
findings.quote: architectural interiors—a large and narrow space respectively—modulate bodily self-consciousness on account of visuo-tactile mechanisms

findings.antecedent: Room's suitability for primed activity and motivations
findings.mechanism: Impressions of space are based on the room's suitability for the primed activity and motivations of the perceiver, indicating a strong dependency between spaciousness and perceived behavioral opportunities.
findings.source: Limitations and Future Directions
findings.quote: user's impressions of space are based on the room's suitability for the primed activity and motivations of the perceiver

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Future studies could investigate the issue of aesthetic stance, as well as experiential and perceptual differences between conscious and unconscious attitudes toward architecture, using distinguished architectural examples as investigative settings.
It might be possible to analyze how spatial structures can act as attentional cues through the mechanism of body schema, including visual, proprioceptive, and tactile stimuli.
Future studies could include phenomenologically-based techniques for obtaining first-person experiential reports in addition to traditional cognitive science methods in VR research.

The 'environmental salience hypothesis' (room design invites/guides activities) and the 'behavioral primacy hypothesis' (impressions of spaciousness influenced by behavioral opportunities) can be tested using IVR paradigms.
The degree of similarity and differences in user experience between immersive virtual reality tools and real environments needs to be systematically examined.
bridge_warrants: The enactive approach acknowledges the common ground between neuroscience and architecture, allowing a more accurate definition of investigative goals.
The enactive perspective has a strong foothold in phenomenological thinking, corresponding to existing phenomenological discourse in architectural theory (Merleau-Ponty, Pallasmaa, Zumthor).
The framework connects neuroscientific findings (e.g., motor system activation, emotion processing) with architectural theory (e.g., Pallasmaa's 'verb form' of architecture).
It integrates Space Syntax methodology by considering configurational properties in relation to embodied experience and affordances, moving beyond purely topological analysis.
The framework builds upon neuroaesthetic research (Freedberg and Gallese) by extending embodied simulation to architectural experience.
methodological_critiques: Existing approaches often emphasize interpreting architectural spaces in terms of objects with quantifiable properties, transforming the perceiver into a disembodied observer.
Space Syntax methodology has been limited in directly linking emotional and aesthetic responses to other than configurational properties.
O'Regan and Noë's sensorimotor contingencies approach supports a narrow view of embodiment, neglecting motor intentionality and affective states.
Current VR research lacks exhaustive studies on the extent to which user's experiences are analogous in virtual and real environments.
Most VR studies rely on rating scales and adjective-based evaluation questionnaires, lacking phenomenologically-based first-person experiential reports.
model_structure: The proposed model (Figure 2) depicts the enactive approach to architectural experience as an interactive interface between body and architecture. This interface is composed of three dynamically interacting layers: 'Constitutive Relatedness' (linking body and cognitive activity), 'Embodied Action' (sensorimotor coupling of perception and action), and 'Sense-making' (cognitive beings as self-individuating and sense-producing systems). These layers influence the human being through 'Body Schema' and 'Affect' components, and interact with 'Affordances' provided by 'Architecture'.
limitations: The fine dynamic interconnection among cerebral networks (sensory-motor, emotion-evaluation, meaning-knowledge) still remains to be investigated in detail.
The enactive concept of presence and emotion in VR has received little to no attention thus far.
The degree of similarity and differences in user experience between immersive virtual reality tools and real environments needs further examination.
The outlined model is a moderate simplification for the purposes of architectural discussion.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Architectural experience is a dynamic, sensorimotor coupling between an embodied agent and the built environment, emphasizing the co-constitution of agent and environment.
The built environment is perceived in terms of its affordances, which are opportunities for action directly perceived by an embodied agent.

mechanism_chain.description: The enactive mechanism for architectural experience, where environmental features afford actions that shape embodied and motivated experience.

steps.to_construct: Embodied architectural experience (including affect and motivation)
